[[File:Burnley_F.C._1920-21.jpg | thumb | right | alt=The team photograph of the Championship-winning Burnley F.C. side in the 1920-21 season | The team photograph of the Championship-winning Burnley F.C. side in the 1920-21 season]]
The '''[[1920 in association football|1920]]–[[1921 in association football|21]] season''' was the 29th season of [[The Football League]].

The [[Football League Third Division]] was introduced, in effect the [[Football League Third Division South|Third Division South]] of the following season, when [[Football League Third Division South|Third Division North]] was introduced. This expanded the League's operational radius all the way to the south coast of England, as the number of member clubs increased from 44 to 66.

==Team changes==
The new Third Division was formed by clubs of the [[1919–20 Southern Football League#Division One|Southern Football League Division One]] of the previous season, except for Cardiff City.  [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] became the first [[Wales|Welsh]] club to enter the League, and since they were the strongest club in Wales in the era, they were invited directly into the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]]. [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]] took its place in the new Third Division, thereby being the first club relegated to the League's third tier. [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] were also elected into the Second Division to replace [[Leeds City F.C.|Leeds City]] after its debacle. [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]] were not re-elected to the Second Division and thus [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]]'s Second Division place was formalized as well.

==Final league tables==
Beginning in the 1894–95 season, clubs finishing level on points were separated according to goal average (goals scored divided by goals conceded). In case one or more teams had the same goal difference, this system favoured those teams who had scored fewer goals. The goal average system was eventually scrapped beginning with the 1976–77 season.

During the first six seasons of the league, (up to the 1893–94 season), re-election process concerned the clubs which finished in the bottom four of the league. From the 1894–95 season and until the 1920–21 season the re-election process was required of the clubs which finished in the bottom three of the league.
